items.question: Do access tokens carry an expiration (exp) and live for minutes rather than days?
items.look_for: Token creation code (Jwts.builder, JwtEncoder, NimbusJwtEncoder) and where the lifetime is configured; any literal lifetime above one hour.
items.source: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet (JWT section); JJWT reference: JwtBuilder.expiration()

items.question: Is a refresh token single-use: every refresh issues a new refresh token and invalidates the old one?
items.look_for: The refresh service or endpoint: after a successful refresh the old token is marked revoked or deleted and a new one is returned.
items.source: OWASP OAuth 2.0 Cheat Sheet (refresh token rotation); Spring Authorization Server: TokenSettings.reuseRefreshTokens

items.question: If an already-used refresh token is presented again, is that detected and are the related tokens revoked?
items.look_for: The branch of the refresh service for a token that is already revoked: does it only reject, or does it also revoke the token family or session?
items.source: OWASP OAuth 2.0 Cheat Sheet (rotation to detect replay); Spring Authorization Server: OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticationProvider (invalidates issued tokens on code reuse)

items.question: Are the check and the revocation of a refresh token atomic, so two concurrent requests with the same token cannot both succeed?
items.look_for: A lock on the lookup (@Lock PESSIMISTIC_WRITE), an @Version column, a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE revoked = false whose updated row count is checked, or a unique constraint on the replacement token.
items.source: Spring Data JPA reference: Locking (@Lock); OWASP OAuth 2.0 Cheat Sheet (refresh token rotation)

items.question: Does logout invalidate the server-side session or revoke the refresh token, not only delete it on the client?
items.look_for: The logout handler or endpoint and what it does to stored sessions or refresh tokens.
items.source: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet (server-side invalidation); OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet (JWT section)

items.question: Does JWT validation use a configured algorithm and key (never the token header), reject unsigned tokens and check expiration?
items.look_for: JwtDecoder / parser configuration: algorithm, key, calls that accept unsecured tokens, exp enforcement.
items.source: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet (JWT section)

items.question: Are the issuer (iss) and audience (aud) of a JWT validated?
items.look_for: Validators attached to the decoder or parser (issuer and audience checks).
items.source: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet (JWT section)

items.question: Is the signing key loaded from configuration or a secret store rather than written in the source?
items.look_for: Where the key or secret is created: literal in code, property placeholder, secret store.
items.source: Spring Boot reference: Externalized Configuration; OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet

items.question: Are repeated failed logins throttled or temporarily locked out?
items.look_for: Login handler or filter: failed-attempt counter, lockout, delay, or an upstream limiter on the login path.
items.source: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet (Login Throttling)

items.question: Do login and registration responses stay the same whether or not the user exists?
items.look_for: Error messages and status codes of the login and registration flows for unknown users versus wrong passwords.
items.source: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet (generic error messages)

items.question: Are password reset tokens single-use and short-lived, and does the reset response stay the same for unknown accounts?
items.look_for: Reset token creation, expiry and consumption; response when the email is unknown.
items.source: OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet

items.question: Does changing the password require the current password?
items.look_for: The change-password endpoint or service.
items.source: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet

items.question: Is there a global rate limit on the API that answers 429 when exceeded?
items.look_for: Filter, gateway or library limiting requests per client; the status code returned.
items.source: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet (429 Too Many Requests); OWASP Denial of Service Cheat Sheet (rate limiting)

items.question: Does the login endpoint have its own, stricter limit?
items.look_for: A limit keyed to the login path or to the username or IP, tighter than the global one.
items.source: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet (Login Throttling); OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet

items.question: Are token refresh, password reset and registration endpoints rate limited too?
items.look_for: Limits on the refresh, reset and sign-up paths.
items.source: OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet; OWASP Denial of Service Cheat Sheet (rate limiting)

items.question: Do the authorization rules deny by default (anyRequest().authenticated() or denyAll())?
items.look_for: The last rule of every SecurityFilterChain and any permitAll on broad patterns.
items.source: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet (Deny by Default); Spring Security 7.0 reference: Authorize HttpServletRequests

items.question: Do endpoints that take an object id check that the object belongs to, or is allowed for, the caller?
items.look_for: Controllers and services with {id} parameters: ownership or permission checks before reading or changing the object (IDOR).
items.source: OWASP Insecure Direct Object Reference Prevention Cheat Sheet

items.question: Are sensitive service methods protected by method security or an equivalent check, not only by URL rules?
items.look_for: @PreAuthorize or explicit checks on service methods that are reachable from several controllers or jobs.
items.source: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet (validate permissions on every request); Spring Security reference: Method Security

items.question: Do request bodies bind to DTOs that contain only editable fields, not directly to entities?
items.look_for: @RequestBody parameter types: entities with sensitive fields (role, admin, balance) versus dedicated DTOs.
items.source: OWASP Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet

items.question: If cookies carry the session or token, are Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite set?
items.look_for: Cookie creation code and the server.servlet.session.cookie.* properties.
items.source: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet; Spring Boot application properties: server.servlet.session.cookie.*

items.question: Does CSRF protection match the authentication model (on for cookie sessions; off only for token-only APIs)?
items.look_for: csrf() configuration, session policy and whether authentication travels in cookies or in an Authorization header.
items.source: OWASP Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet

items.question: Does CORS allow only the real front-end origins?
items.look_for: CorsConfiguration, @CrossOrigin and WebMvcConfigurer.addCorsMappings: wildcard origins, credentials.
items.source: Spring Framework reference: Web MVC CORS

items.question: Are passwords stored with an adaptive encoder (BCrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2, SCrypt) through PasswordEncoder, with upgrade support?
items.look_for: PasswordEncoder beans and where passwords are hashed.
items.source: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet; Spring Security 7.0 reference: Password Storage

items.question: Are long passwords accepted (at least 64 characters) and never silently truncated?
items.look_for: Validation rules on password length at registration and change.
items.source: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet

items.question: Do secrets (database, keys, API tokens) come from the environment or a secret store?
items.look_for: application*.yml / properties, @Value and code constants holding credentials.
items.source: Spring Boot reference: Externalized Configuration; OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet

items.question: Are actuator endpoints limited to what is needed and secured?
items.look_for: management.endpoints.web.exposure.* and the authorization rules covering /actuator.
items.source: Spring Boot reference: Actuator, Endpoints > Security

items.question: Are HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and a frame protection header sent?
items.look_for: headers() configuration, reverse proxy configuration.
items.source: OWASP HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet

items.question: Is HTTPS enforced on all pages, directly or at a proxy?
items.look_for: requiresChannel, server.ssl.*, proxy or ingress settings.
items.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet (Use TLS For All Pages)

items.question: Are request bodies validated on the server (@Valid with constraints)?
items.look_for: @Valid / @Validated on controller parameters and constraints on the DTOs.
items.source: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet

items.question: Do error responses avoid stack traces and internal details?
items.look_for: Global exception handlers, server.error.* properties, custom error bodies.
items.source: Spring Boot reference: Error Handling (server.error.include-stacktrace, default never)

items.question: Are authentication successes and failures and access-denied events logged?
items.look_for: Event listeners (AuthenticationSuccessEvent, AuthorizationDeniedEvent), handlers and log statements in security code.
items.source: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
